Class 12 Chemistry · Chemical Kinetics (first-order reactions, half-life)
Chemistry, visualised #7

Every half-life, half of what's left decays: 64 → 32 → 16 → B.
Which atom goes next is pure chance. How many go is not: radioactive decay is first order, so the half-life (t½ = 0.693/k) is the same however many atoms are left.
That's how carbon dating works: C-14 halves every 5,730 years, so a bone with 25% of its C-14 left is about 11,460 years old.
